body.statement: If \(m\) is even and \((A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\), then \((-A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\). If \(A_{vu}\ne0\), the two attained transfers \(A_{vu}z/(1-A_{vv}z)\) and \(-A_{vu}z/(1+A_{vv}z)\) are unequal as rational functions. Hence no nonzero queried edge transfer is point identified from the Gaussian coarse law under an even factor.
body.justification: The global sign action is an unavoidable same-law obstruction that covariance filtering cannot remove.
body.gap: Gong et al.'s even sign conclusion is embedded in a non-Gaussian identification theorem; this claim proves the obstruction directly for the Gaussian law after the complete coarse covariance restriction.
body.consumer: For a conditionally ordered Temperature--Ozone analysis with \(m=2\), the result prevents reporting a branch-selected directional transfer as identified.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(m\) be even.  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}known\mbox{-}sampling\mbox{-}factor}\), \(m\) is the fixed subsampling factor and \(m\geq 2\), so there is an integer \(k\geq 1\) such that \(m=2k\).  Fix \((A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\), and put \(\widetilde A=-A\).  The defining equalities in \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\mbox{-}fiber}\) first give
\[
 \widetilde A^{,m}=(-A)^{2k}=A^{2k}=A^m=B.
\]
For every \(r\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\), scalar multiplication commutes with matrix powers and transposition, whence
\[
 \widetilde A^{,r}D(\widetilde A^{,r})^\top
 =(-1)^rA^rD\bigl((-1)^rA^r\bigr)^\top
 =(-1)^{2r}A^rD(A^r)^\top
 =A^rD(A^r)^\top.
\]
Summation and the covariance equality in \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\mbox{-}fiber}\) therefore yield
\[
 \sum_{r=0}^{m-1}\widetilde A^{,r}D(\widetilde A^{,r})^\top
 =\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A^rD(A^r)^\top
 =Q.
\]
All zero restrictions are preserved because \(\widetilde A_{ij}=-A_{ij}\): in particular, \(\widetilde A_{ij}=0\) whenever \(i<j\), and also whenever \(i>j\) but \(j\to i\notin G\).  The diagonal stability restriction is preserved since
\[
 \max_i|\widetilde A_{ii}|=\max_i|-A_{ii}|=\max_i|A_{ii}|<1.
\]
Finally, \(D\) is unchanged, so it remains diagonal and positive definite.  These checks exhaust the defining constraints of \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\); hence
\[
 (-A,D)=(\widetilde A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G).
\]

For completeness, the equality just proved is equality of the full stationary coarse Gaussian laws, not only equality of two displayed parameters.  For \(s\in\{1,-1\}\), set \(A_s=sA\), take an independent sequence \((\varepsilon_t^{(s)})_{t\in\mathbb Z}\) with law \(N(0,D)\), and form the stationary Gaussian recursion
\[
 X_t^{(s)}=A_sX_{t-1}^{(s)}+\varepsilon_t^{(s)}.
\]
This stationary process exists because \(A_s\) is triangular and
\(\rho(A_s)=\max_i|(A_s)_{ii}|<1\); explicitly, the series
\(X_t^{(s)}=\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}A_s^\ell\varepsilon_{t-\ell}^{(s)}\)
converges in second mean.  Iterating the recursion over one sampling block and writing \(Y_j^{(s)}=X_{jm}^{(s)}\) gives
\[
 Y_j^{(s)}=A_s^mY_{j-1}^{(s)}+\eta_j^{(s)},
 \qquad
 \eta_j^{(s)}=\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A_s^r\varepsilon_{jm-r}^{(s)}.
\]
Different \(j\)'s use disjoint innovation blocks, so the variables \(\eta_j^{(s)}\) are independent; they are centered Gaussian and independent of the preceding coarse history.  The two calculations above imply, for both signs \(s\),
\[
 A_s^m=B,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(\eta_j^{(s)})
 =\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A_s^rD(A_s^r)^\top=Q.
\]
Moreover \(\rho(B)=\rho(A)^m<1\), so the stationary covariance of either coarse process is the convergent series
\[
 \Gamma_0=\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}B^\ell Q(B^\ell)^\top.
\]
Thus both sampled processes have the same stationary initial law \(N(0,\Gamma_0)\), the same transition matrix \(B\), and independent innovations with the same law \(N(0,Q)\).  Recursive conditioning therefore gives equality of all their finite-dimensional distributions.  This proves the asserted same-law property even after the complete coarse covariance restriction is imposed.

It remains to show that the same law can carry two different queried transfers.  The assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}query\mbox{-}edge}\) fixes \(u\to v\) as the queried process-DAG arrow.  Write \(p=A_{vu}\) and \(q=A_{vv}\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}transfer\mbox{-}fiber}\), the points \((A,D)\) and \((-A,D)\) found above contribute, respectively,
\[
 h_+(z)=\frac{pz}{1-qz}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 h_-(z)=\frac{-pz}{1+qz}
\]
to \(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)\).  Since \(|q|<1\), both denominators are nonzero for every \(z\in\mathbb T\).  If these rational functions were equal, cross-multiplication would give the polynomial identity
\[
 pz(1+qz)=-pz(1-qz),
 \qquad\text{and hence}\qquad
 2pz=0.
\]
This is impossible when \(p=A_{vu}\neq0\).  Consequently \(h_+\neq h_-\), and both are attained elements of the same transfer fiber.  That fiber is therefore not a singleton.  Because the two compatible Gaussian structural models induce exactly the same observed coarse law, no functional of that law can equal the nonzero queried fine-grid transfer in both models; point identification fails.
